paragraphs: A clownfish is three white bars on orange, edged in black, and the bars are what everyone checks. Their width, their curve and where they sit relative to the fins vary between species, and getting them wrong turns the fish into a generic tropical. The body itself is stubby with rounded fins, built for hovering in an anemone rather than for open water speed.

The mesh is minimal at 4,659 polygons and 4,637 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 6 texture maps at 4096x4096. That balance is right for a small fish, where the pattern does almost all of the work.

This page carries a swimming pose at $59 and a rigged build at $69. Aimed at aquarium and marine visualisation, children's and education content, advertising, film and television, and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2016.

A man portable air defence missile is carried and fired from the shoulder, which sets everything about it: a launch tube sized to be lifted by one soldier, a gripstock with a trigger and battery unit beneath, an open sight frame that folds up, and a separable eyepiece. The gripstock is reused; the tube is not.

The mesh runs 147,241 polygons and 148,025 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 12 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the stencilled instructions and the wear on the grip.

At $59 it suits defence and conflict visualisation, news and documentary graphics, film and television armouries, training material and games. Real-world scale is kept, so it fits a character's shoulder correctly. On sale since 2017.

A whole cured ham on its stand is an object of display as much as of food. The leg keeps the hoof, the fat cap is scored, the meat darkens toward the bone, and the wooden clamp holds it at the angle a carver needs. That whole arrangement is a fixture of Spanish delicatessens and restaurant counters.

The mesh is minimal at 2,859 polygons and 2,893 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is exactly right for a subject whose realism lives in the texture: the fat marbling, the cure and the wood grain.

At $59 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits food and delicatessen visualisation, restaurant and menu imagery, gourmet and specialty retail renders, food photography set dressing, and games. On sale since 2025.

A machine operator's seat is a control station: the chair itself on a suspension base, with armrest pods carrying joysticks, switches and often a display. Those pods move with the seat rather than with the cab, so the controls stay under the hands however the seat is adjusted, and that relationship has to be modelled correctly.
The mesh is efficient at 16,222 polygons and 17,289 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, with the geometry in the joystick heads, the switch panels and the suspension base.

At $59 and built to StemCell specification, it suits heavy equipment and cab interior visualisation, machinery marketing and catalogues, operator training material, simulator projects and games. On sale since 2026.

Phone packaging is a product in its own right. The box is a tight two-part sleeve with almost no printing, a matte finish, and a lid that lifts against a controlled vacuum rather than sliding off - which is why unboxing videos exist at all. That restraint is what has to be reproduced, since there is nothing to hide behind.
The mesh is efficient at 26,682 polygons and 27,386 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the lid as a separate body so it can be shown closed, lifting or removed.

This page carries white, blue and green versions at $59 and a further black build at $79. All suit consumer electronics packaging visualisation, brand and unboxing marketing, retail and e-commerce renders, and games. On sale since 2021.

A cartoon child character has proportions that break every anatomical rule deliberately: an oversized head, tiny hands and feet, and a body reduced to almost nothing under a dress. Those exaggerations are the character, and they have to be committed to fully - a half-stylised figure lands in the uncanny middle where neither audience is served.
This build is delivered in T-pose at 101,436 polygons and 98,915 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is the neutral stance a rig binds to and clothing fits against.

Two rigged builds sit on this page at $79, including a version prepared for Maya. Aimed at animation and children's content, character design and previsualisation, merchandise and print, and games. On sale since 2024.

Cutting a pile off at the seabed is a job done by a machine that clamps around it and works a cutting head circumferentially. This asset supplies both halves of that operation - the cutter and the pile it works on - which is what makes the process legible rather than showing a piece of equipment in isolation.
The mesh runs 174,678 polygons and 187,803 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, a sound economy on machinery built from repeated clamp segments and identical hydraulics.

At $59 and built to StemCell specification, it suits offshore energy and decommissioning visualisation, subsea engineering presentation, renewables and oil industry marketing, technical documentation and games. On sale since 2025.

An outdoor court is not an indoor one with the roof removed. The surface is asphalt or painted concrete rather than sprung wood, the hoops are on single posts with padded backboards, there is usually a fence around it, and the line paint is worn where players actually stand. Those differences are what make it read as a public court.

The mesh runs 237,916 polygons and 244,006 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 12 texture maps at a mix of sizes up to 4096x4096 carrying the surface wear, the line paint and the fence.
At $59 it suits urban and community visualisation, sports and lifestyle advertising, architectural and landscape renders, film and television, and games. On sale since 2019.

A supersonic demonstrator is built to prove a shape rather than to carry anyone, which is why this aircraft is so slim: a long pointed nose, a delta planform, three small engines and a cockpit so buried that the pilot uses a camera to see forward on approach. Every proportion serves wave drag rather than comfort.
The mesh runs 200,789 polygons and 106,596 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the intake lips, the wing leading edge and the tail.

This page is unusually deep, with seven other builds from $59 to $79 including dark grey variants and rigged versions prepared for Maya and Cinema 4D. Aimed at aerospace marketing, aviation journalism, future transport presentation, documentary work and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2024.

Showing a dispenser in use rather than idle changes what the object communicates. The lever is depressed, the nozzle is dispensing, and the scene becomes about hygiene practice rather than about wall-mounted hardware. That distinction matters in healthcare and public health material where behaviour is the message.

The mesh is light at 14,125 polygons and 14,686 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, sensible on a symmetrical moulded housing, and the CheckMate build keeps the surfacing clean for close product renders.
At $59 it suits healthcare and public health visualisation, hospital and clinic interiors, facility management and hygiene marketing, workplace safety material, and games. On sale since 2026.

This rifle was designed around silence rather than around a cartridge. The barrel is ported into an integral suppressor that runs most of the weapon's length, which is why the barrel appears so thick and why the front sight sits on the suppressor body rather than on the barrel itself. The wooden thumbhole stock is the other identifier.

The mesh runs 77,010 polygons and 78,305 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 12 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the parkerised metal, the wood grain and the handling wear.

At $59 it suits military and special operations visualisation, film and television armouries, games, documentary work and training material. Real-world scale is kept, so it fits a character rig. On sale since 2016.

A demountable grandstand is a scaffold structure with seating decks bolted onto it, a roof over the top and stairs at each end. It exists to be assembled for an event and taken away afterwards, which is why every joint is visible and nothing is clad - and that exposed structure is what makes it read as temporary rather than as a stadium.
The mesh runs 161,794 polygons and 169,478 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the frame members and the seating rows.

At $59 and built to StemCell specification, it suits event and venue visualisation, sports and festival presentation, temporary infrastructure planning, film and television set dressing, and games. On sale since 2023.

An electric drive unit combines motor, inverter and reduction gearbox in one casing, which is why it looks so unlike an engine and transmission: a compact aluminium package with the driveshafts emerging from either side and high voltage connectors on top. The absence of an exhaust, a sump or a bellhousing is the whole point.
The mesh is efficient at 22,137 polygons and 24,090 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the casing ribs, the connectors and the mounting points.

At $59 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits automotive engineering and technology marketing, electric vehicle presentation, technical cutaways, education and training material, and games. On sale since 2025.

Watertight doors are heavy steel plates in a raised coaming, with dogs around the frame that clamp them shut and a handle that operates all of them at once. Ships need several types - quick acting, sliding, and lighter weathertight versions - and a corridor or a bulkhead dressed with only one of them looks wrong to anyone who has been aboard.
Supplying them as a collection keeps the coaming heights and the hardware consistent between doors, which is exactly what goes wrong when a ship interior is assembled from separate sources.

A second collection sits on this page at $79. This set at $59 is aimed at marine and naval interior visualisation, shipbuilding and offshore presentation, film and television set dressing, training material and games. Built to CheckMate specification, on sale since 2025.
